reason: The hypothesis relies on a chain of premises linking SRO to altered creep mechanisms, but the cited evidence provides only indirect or partial support. E1 and E6 establish that SRO exists in HEAs and can influence strain fields, but do not address interfacial SRO in multilayers or its effect on creep. E3 shows a stress-dependent transition from diffusion to dislocation creep in bulk HEAs, but does not link this to SRO. E5 shows HEA complexity restricts dislocation motion, but not via SRO. No cited evidence directly supports the claim that annealing enhances interfacial SRO to raise dislocation
premises: Chemical short-range order (SRO) can be enhanced at FCC/BCC interfaces in HEA multilayers by controlled annealing.
Enhanced interfacial SRO locally increases lattice distortion and heterogeneity.
Increased lattice distortion/heterogeneity from SRO raises the activation barrier for dislocation nucleation and glide.
Raising the dislocation nucleation/glide barrier governs a transition from diffusion-controlled to dislocation-mediated creep.
This mechanism results in a higher creep stress exponent and lower creep strain rate compared to a low-SRO baseline.
